why_en: Auth, friend management, likes, and compliance are explicitly out of scope, so digging into them wastes time needed for offline, local stats, and storage.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确把社交 feed 或隐私合规设为核心需求，就应重新调整设计重点。
tradeoff: 把时间投入核心非功能需求 vs 深挖范围外细节

termDefinitions.meaning: 欧盟的数据隐私保护法规，要求企业合规处理用户数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GDPR is the EU data-privacy regulation that requires companies to handle user data in compliant ways.

optionExplanations: 离线记录是题目明确的核心非功能需求，越早讲清楚越能体现对 availability 的把控，不该被砍。
路线数据量级直接决定分片、归档这些基础设施判断，是支撑存储设计的必答内容。
暂停/恢复和 active time 计算依赖状态日志建模，这是 elapsed-time 这类核心功能问题绕不开的部分。
认证、好友管理增删、点赞评论、GDPR 都被题目明确划在范围外，深挖它们只会挤占核心非功能需求的时间。
optionExplanations_en: Offline recording is a requirement the prompt explicitly calls core; covering it early demonstrates command of availability and should not be cut.
Route data volume directly drives sharding and archiving decisions, so it is required content for supporting the storage design.
Pause/resume and active-time math depend on state-log modeling, an unavoidable part of the elapsed-time problem this design has to solve.
Auth, friend management, likes/comments, and GDPR are all explicitly out of scope in the prompt, so digging into them only eats time needed for the core non-functional requirements.

scenario: 题目给定的非功能目标是系统要同时支撑 1000 万个进行中的活动，设备每约 3 秒采一个 GPS 点。
scenario_en: The prompt gives a non-functional target of supporting 10 million concurrent in-progress activities, with devices sampling a GPS point about every 3 seconds.
q: 1000 万并发活动这个目标，最先约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Which design path does the 10-million-concurrent-activities target constrain first?
options: 它是从写吞吐反推出来的结果，用于定副本数量
它决定 GPS 采样精度，和后端写路径无关
它决定活动记录放客户端还是持续回传服务端
它决定好友关系表要不要加二级索引
options_en: It is a result derived from write throughput, used to size the replica count
It sets GPS sampling accuracy and has nothing to do with the backend write path
It decides whether recording lives on the client or streams to the server
It decides whether the friends table needs a secondary index
why: 这是题目给定的产品目标，不是公式推导出来的结果；它约束写路径——后端写入 = 并发活动数 ÷ 上报间隔 = 1000万 ÷ 3秒 ≈ 每秒 330 万次，逼着记录留在设备上。
why_en: Ten million concurrent activities is a given product target, not a derived number, and it constrains the write path: concurrent activities divided by the reporting interval is ten million over three seconds, roughly three point three million writes per second, which forces recording onto the device.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全球定位系统（GPS）：设备通过卫星信号得到自己经纬度坐标的定位系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPS, the Global Positioning System, lets a device work out its own latitude and longitude from satellite signals.

termDefinitions.meaning: 二级索引：建在主键之外的字段上、用来加速按该字段查询的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A secondary index is an index built on a non-primary-key column so queries can filter on that column quickly.

optionExplanations: 误解：它是题目直接给的产品目标，不是从任何吞吐公式反推出来的中间量。
误解：采样精度由电量和运动类型决定，和要撑多少并发活动是两个问题。
并发数 ÷ 上报间隔就是后端每秒写入量，量级大到只能把记录留在设备上。
误解：好友表的索引由读查询形态决定，和进行中活动的并发规模无关。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: it is a product target stated in the prompt, not an intermediate value back-computed from any throughput formula.
Misconception: sampling accuracy is driven by battery and activity type, a separate question from how many concurrent activities to support.
Concurrency divided by reporting interval is the backend write rate per second, and that magnitude forces recording onto the device.
Misconception: the friends-table index is shaped by read queries, not by the number of activities in progress.

scenario: App 每约 10 秒把内存 buffer 落盘到本地存储。用户跑到一半 App 被系统杀掉，重开后继续记录同一次活动。
scenario_en: The app flushes its in-memory buffer to local storage about every 10 seconds. Mid-run the app is killed by the OS, and the user reopens it to keep recording the same activity.
q: 重开后直接用空 buffer 继续记录，会坏在哪一步？
q_en: Where does it break if recording resumes with an empty buffer after reopening?
options: GPS 采样频率会被系统自动降到最低档
服务端会把这次活动判定为重复提交，整段路线被拒绝写入
前半段的点留在本地存储没被载回，最终只上传后半段
本地存储写满后会拒绝新的落盘请求
options_en: The OS automatically drops GPS sampling to its lowest frequency
The server treats the activity as a duplicate submission and rejects the whole route
The earlier points stay in local storage and never get reloaded, so only the second half uploads
Local storage fills up and starts rejecting new flushes
why: 恢复流程要求重开时先读本地存储、回填 buffer 再记新点；跳过这步，内存里只剩重开后的点，上传出去的路线就缺了前半段。代价只是启动时多一次本地读。
why_en: On resume you have to read local storage back into the buffer before recording new points; skip that and memory only holds the points after the restart, so the uploaded route is missing its first half. The cost is just one extra local read at startup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存 buffer：先把最新采到的数据暂存在内存里，再周期性写入本地存储的缓冲区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-memory buffer holds freshly captured data in RAM before it is periodically written to local storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全球定位系统（GPS）：设备通过卫星信号得到自己经纬度坐标的定位系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GPS, the Global Positioning System, lets a device work out its own latitude and longitude from satellite signals.

optionExplanations: 误解：采样频率由 App 的定位配置决定，被杀死重启不会让系统改写它。
误解：重复提交要有两次完整上传才会发生，这里根本没有第二份数据。
落盘过的点还躺在本地存储里，没人把它读回内存，保存时只有重启后的坐标进入上传包，用户看到距离从零重算。
误解：本地存储写满是容量问题，和重启时要不要回填 buffer 是两条独立路径。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: sampling frequency comes from the app's location configuration; being killed and restarted does not make the OS rewrite it.
Misconception: a duplicate submission needs two complete uploads, and here there is no second copy at all.
The flushed points still sit in local storage with nobody reading them back, so only post-restart coordinates enter the upload and distance restarts from zero.
Misconception: running out of local storage is a capacity problem, separate from whether the buffer gets refilled on restart.

scenario: 离线优先设计默认活动结束才上传。一次 4 小时长骑行中途，手机重新进入有信号的区域。
scenario_en: The offline-first design uploads only when an activity ends. Midway through a four-hour ride, the phone comes back into network coverage.
q: 活动还没结束时，客户端该怎么处理已积累的数据？
q_en: What should the client do with accumulated data while the activity is still running?
options: 保持只在活动结束时上传，中途一律不动
有网就在后台机会性上传已积累的分段
改回每 2-5 秒实时上报服务端
把 buffer 复制到第二块本地存储再等结束
options_en: Keep uploading only when the activity ends and touch nothing in between
Opportunistically upload the accumulated chunk in the background when a connection appears
Switch back to pushing to the server every 2 to 5 seconds
Copy the buffer into a second local store and still wait for the end
why: 耐久性 vs 带宽：只等结束上传，4 小时的点全押在一台可能掉电的手机上；有网时机会性后台同步先把一部分数据搬到服务端，代价是多几次请求和电量。
why_en: It's durability versus bandwidth: waiting until the end bets four hours of data on one phone that may die, while opportunistic background sync moves part of it to the server whenever a connection exists, at the cost of extra requests and battery.
tradeoff: 数据耐久性 vs 请求次数与电量开销
whenOtherWins: 活动很短、或设备整程都没有信号时，只在结束时上传一次更省电，也省掉服务端合并分段的复杂度。

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存 buffer：先把最新采到的数据暂存在内存里，再周期性写入本地存储的缓冲区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-memory buffer holds freshly captured data in RAM before it is periodically written to local storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机会性同步：不固定时刻上传，而是在网络恰好可用时把已有数据推送出去。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Opportunistic sync means uploading whenever a network connection happens to be available, rather than on a fixed schedule.

optionExplanations: 端到端只有一次上传点，手机掉电或损坏时这 4 小时数据没有任何服务端副本。
有信号就把已积累的分段推上去，掉电时服务端至少已有前面那部分。
这等于放弃离线优先，把写量重新加回后端，正是这道题一开始要避开的成本。
误解：第二份本地副本挡不住整机掉电或丢失，副本要放到另一台机器才算耐久。
optionExplanations_en: There is only one upload point end to end, so a dead or broken phone leaves four hours of data with no server-side copy.
When a signal appears the accumulated chunk goes up, so a dead battery still leaves the earlier portion on the server.
This abandons offline-first and puts the write load back on the backend, exactly the cost this design set out to avoid.
Misconception: a second local copy does not survive the whole device dying or being lost; durability needs a copy on another machine.

scenario: 客户端上传完活动后要清掉本地 buffer 释放空间。弱网下请求可能超时，响应也可能丢失。
scenario_en: After uploading an activity the client wants to clear its local buffer to free space, but on a weak network the request can time out and the response can be lost.
q: 发出上传请求就立刻删本地 buffer，会坏成什么样？
q_en: What breaks if the client deletes the local buffer the moment it sends the upload request?
options: 服务端会收到两份相同活动，产生重复记录
请求在网络中失败时本地已无副本，这段活动彻底丢失
本地存储空间会被写满，导致无法继续采集坐标
服务端保存成功但客户端仍认为活动没结束，一直卡在进行中
options_en: The server receives two copies of the same activity and creates duplicate records
If the request fails in flight there is no local copy left, so the activity is gone for good
Local storage fills up and coordinate capture cannot continue
The server saves successfully but the client still thinks the activity is unfinished and stays stuck in progress
why: 同步生命周期的终点是服务端返回保存确认，不是请求发出的那一刻；提前删除等于把唯一副本押在一次可能超时的请求上。代价是本地空间要一直占到确认到达。
why_en: The sync lifecycle ends when the server confirms the save, not when the request leaves the phone; deleting early bets the only copy on a request that may time out. The cost is holding local space until that confirmation arrives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内存 buffer：先把最新采到的数据暂存在内存里，再周期性写入本地存储的缓冲区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An in-memory buffer holds freshly captured data in RAM before it is periodically written to local storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存确认：服务端明确回复数据已经写入远端数据库的那个响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A save confirmation is the response in which the server explicitly states the data has been written to the remote database.

optionExplanations: 误解：重复记录来自确认丢失后的重试，正是保留 buffer 才可能出现的问题，不是提前删除的后果。
请求超时、服务端 5xx 或响应丢包时都无法重试，因为可重传的数据已经被自己删掉了。
误解：删得太早是空间被过早释放，方向恰好相反，不会撑满存储。
误解：活动状态由 PATCH 到 COMPLETE 决定，和本地 buffer 什么时候删没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: duplicate records come from retrying after a lost confirmation, which is a risk of keeping the buffer, not of deleting it early.
On a timeout, a server 5xx, or a dropped response there is nothing to retry with, because the retransmittable data was already deleted.
Misconception: deleting too early frees space too soon, the opposite direction, so it cannot fill storage.
Misconception: activity state is driven by the PATCH to COMPLETE and is unrelated to when the local buffer is deleted.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  B[Local buffer owns data]
  U[Upload request sent]
  A{Server save confirmed?}
  D[Delete local buffer]
  R[Keep buffer and retry]
  B --> U --> A
  A -- yes --> D
  A -- no or timeout --> R --> U

scenario: 活动数据一年约 547.5TB，写入是活动完成时的一次批量提交，读吞吐很低，字段之间关系很弱。
scenario_en: Activity data grows to roughly 547.5 terabytes a year, writes arrive as one batch when an activity completes, read throughput is low, and the data is only weakly relational.
q: 被问到该选哪种数据库时，最合理的回答是什么？
q_en: When asked which database to pick here, what is the most reasonable answer?
options: 必须用时序数据库，否则坐标点写不进去
主流数据库都能胜任，重点在分片与冷热分层
必须用图数据库来承载好友关系查询
必须选宽列存储，因为一年数据超过 500TB
options_en: You must use a time-series database or the coordinate points cannot be written
Any mainstream database works; the real work is sharding and hot/cold tiering
You must use a graph database to serve friend-relationship queries
You must pick a wide-column store because the yearly data exceeds 500 terabytes
why: 量大但可控、吞吐不高、关系性弱，这三条没有把任何一类数据库排除掉，所以选型不是本题的得分点；真正要花时间的是按完成时间分片和把旧活动分层到便宜存储。
why_en: The data is large but manageable, throughput is modest, and the relationships are weak, so none of the mainstream engines is ruled out and the choice itself is not where points are won; sharding by completion time and tiering old activities is.
tradeoff: 纠结数据库品牌 vs 把时间花在分片与分层
whenOtherWins: 如果需求改成高频写入实时轨迹或复杂社交图多跳遍历，时序库或图数据库的专用索引才真正开始领先。

termDefinitions.meaning: 时序数据库：为按时间戳高频追加写和时间范围查询专门优化的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-series database is optimized for high-frequency appends keyed by timestamp and for time-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 图数据库：把实体和实体之间的关系当作一等公民存储、擅长多跳关系遍历的数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A graph database stores entities and the relationships between them as first-class objects and excels at multi-hop traversal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 宽列存储：按列族组织数据、面向超大规模写入横向扩展的存储引擎，如 Cassandra。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A wide-column store organizes data into column families and scales horizontally for very large write volumes, like Cassandra.

optionExplanations: 误解：坐标点带时间戳不等于必须上时序引擎，普通表加索引在这个写入频率下完全够。
三条约束都不极端，选型空间被留得很宽，判断力体现在分片键和分层策略上。
误解：好友查询是一跳的 (userId, friendId) 查表，普通索引就能覆盖，用不上图遍历。
误解：总量大不等于单点压力大，写入是完成时一次批量，不需要专为写扩展的引擎。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: timestamped coordinates do not require a time-series engine; an ordinary indexed table handles this write rate fine.
None of the three constraints is extreme, so the engine choice stays wide open and the judgment shows up in shard key and tiering.
Misconception: friend lookup is a one-hop query on (userId, friendId) that an ordinary index covers, with no traversal needed.
Misconception: a large total does not mean high per-write pressure; writes arrive as one batch at completion.

scenario: 排行榜改成后台作业定期把新活动汇总进一张 leaderboard 表，查询只做一次排序读取。
scenario_en: The leaderboard is now maintained by a background job that periodically rolls new activities into a leaderboard table, so a query is one sorted read.
q: 决定这个汇总作业的运行频率时，取舍轴是什么？
q_en: What is the tradeoff axis when choosing how often the aggregation job runs?
options: 频率只影响 Redis 的内存占用，与数据库无关
越频繁越好，汇总作业不会占用主库资源
太频繁压资源，太稀疏则排行榜陈旧
频率无关紧要，因为读的是预先算好的表
options_en: Frequency only affects Redis memory usage and has nothing to do with the database
More often is always better because the job does not consume primary-database resources
Too frequent strains resources; too sparse leaves the leaderboard stale
Frequency does not matter because reads hit a precomputed table
why: 预聚合把查询成本换成了作业成本：跑得越勤，扫描和写回越频繁地压主库资源；跑得越稀，用户越可能看不到自己刚完成的活动。只能按可接受的陈旧度定。
why_en: Pre-aggregation trades query cost for job cost: running it more often means scanning and writing back more often against the primary database, while running it less often means a user may not see the activity they just finished. You pick by the staleness you can accept.
tradeoff: 作业资源开销 vs 排行榜数据新鲜度
whenOtherWins: 如果要求排名在活动完成后立刻更新，就要放弃定期作业，改用 Redis sorted set 在写入时增量加分。

termDefinitions.meaning: 预聚合：提前把明细数据汇总成结果表，查询时直接读结果而不再实时计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-aggregation rolls detail rows into a result table ahead of time so queries read the result instead of computing it live.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 有序集合：每个成员带一个分数、按分数自动排序的结构，取前 N 名很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps each member with a score and orders members by that score, so reading the top N is very fast.

optionExplanations: 误解：这条路径根本没有 Redis，成本落在扫描明细和写回汇总表的数据库开销上。
误解：作业要扫新活动并写汇总行，跑得越勤对主库的读写压力越大。
两端都有代价，只能挑一个用户能忍受的滞后窗口，没有免费的频率。
误解：读便宜正是预聚合的目的，但表里的数字有多旧完全由作业频率决定。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: there is no Redis on this path; the cost lands on scanning detail rows and writing aggregate rows in the database.
Misconception: the job scans new activities and writes aggregate rows, so running it more often loads the primary database more.
Both ends cost something, so you pick a lag window users tolerate; no frequency is free.
Misconception: cheap reads are exactly the point of pre-aggregation, but how stale the numbers are is set entirely by job frequency.

scenario: Strava 题有三条功能需求：记录活动、运动中看数据、看自己和好友的活动，而高层设计只有十几分钟。
scenario_en: The Strava question has three functional requirements — record activities, view live stats, and view your own and friends' activities — and only about fifteen minutes for high-level design.
q: 高层设计阶段就铺开离线 buffer 和 Redis 排行榜，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of unpacking offline buffering and Redis leaderboards during high-level design?
options: 复杂方案本身就是扣分项，面试官只接受最简架构
时间耗在深挖上，三条功能需求还没答完就到点了
提前引入 Redis 会让后面的数据库分片讨论无法进行
客户端逻辑讲得太细会让服务端设计被判定为错误
options_en: A sophisticated design is itself a deduction, since interviewers only accept the simplest architecture
Time goes into deep dives and the three functional requirements are still unanswered when time runs out
Introducing Redis early makes the later database sharding discussion impossible
Explaining client logic in detail causes the server design to be judged wrong
why: 先给最简可行系统、把复杂度留到 deep dive，是为了保证三条功能需求都落地；已经想清楚的复杂方案可以提前讲，代价是必须自己盯住剩下的时间。
why_en: Starting with the simplest system that satisfies the functional requirements and layering complexity in the deep dives is how you guarantee all three requirements get covered; presenting a design you already know well is fine, but then you have to watch the clock yourself.
tradeoff: 高层设计的深度 vs 覆盖全部功能需求
whenOtherWins: 如果三条功能需求都已覆盖、时间还宽裕，提前展开想清楚的复杂方案反而能把深度亮出来。

termDefinitions.meaning: 深挖环节：高层设计讲完后，针对某个非功能需求展开细节论证的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the stage after high-level design where you unpack the details behind one non-functional requirement.

optionExplanations: 误解：成熟的复杂方案本身不扣分，扣分的是它挤掉了功能需求的时间。
十几分钟被一个深挖吃掉，剩下的功能需求只能草草带过，等于没回答问题本身。
误解：排行榜和活动表分片是两条独立的话题，先讲哪个都不会锁死另一个。
误解：客户端承担记录逻辑正是这道题的正确方向，讲细不会让服务端设计变错。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: a well-thought-out sophisticated design is not penalized in itself; what costs you is the requirement time it displaces.
One deep dive eats the fifteen minutes, the remaining requirements get rushed, and the question itself goes unanswered.
Misconception: leaderboards and activity-table sharding are independent topics, and covering one first does not lock out the other.
Misconception: putting recording logic on the client is the right direction here, so detailing it does not make the server design wrong.
